name: Dal Tadka
steps: Rinse the toor dal and pressure-cook with 3 cups of water, turmeric and salt for 3-4 whistles until soft. Whisk until smooth.
Heat 1 tbsp ghee in a pan. Add cumin seeds and asafoetida; when the seeds splutter, add onion, ginger, garlic and green chilli.
Saute until the onion turns golden, then add tomato and red chilli powder. Cook until the tomato softens and the oil separates.
Pour in the cooked dal, mix well and simmer for 5 minutes. Add water if too thick.
For the tadka, heat the remaining ghee, add a few garlic slices and a pinch of red chilli powder, and pour over the dal.
Garnish with coriander leaves and serve hot with rice or roti.

name: Aloo Gobi
steps: Heat oil in a kadhai. Add cumin seeds; when they splutter, add onion, ginger and green chilli and fry until the onion is soft.
Add tomato, turmeric, coriander powder and salt. Cook until the tomato breaks down.
Add potato and cauliflower, mix well to coat with the masala, cover and cook on low for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Sprinkle a little water if the vegetables stick. Cook until the potato is tender and the cauliflower is done but not mushy.
Stir in garam masala and coriander leaves. Serve hot with roti or paratha.

name: Paneer Butter Masala
steps: Boil the tomatoes, onion, garlic, ginger and cashews in 1 cup of water for 10 minutes. Cool and blend to a smooth puree.
Melt butter in a pan, add the puree and cook on medium heat for 10 minutes until it thickens and the oil separates.
Add red chilli powder, garam masala, sugar and salt. Stir in the cream.
Add the paneer cubes and simmer for 5 minutes so they soak up the gravy.
Serve hot with naan, roti or jeera rice.

name: Egg Curry
steps: Peel the boiled eggs and make shallow slits on each so the gravy seeps in.
Heat oil, add onion and fry until golden. Add ginger, garlic and green chilli; fry for a minute.
Add tomato, turmeric, red chilli powder and coriander powder. Cook until the oil separates.
Add 1 cup of water, bring to a boil, then slide in the eggs and simmer for 5 minutes.
Sprinkle garam masala and coriander leaves. Serve with rice or roti.

name: Vegetable Pulao
steps: Heat ghee in a heavy pot. Add cumin seeds and bay leaf; when they crackle, add onion, ginger and green chilli.
Add all the vegetables and fry for 3-4 minutes.
Drain the rice and add it with garam masala and salt. Stir gently for a minute.
Add 3 cups of hot water, cover and cook on low for 15 minutes until the rice is done.
Rest for 5 minutes, fluff with a fork and garnish with coriander leaves. Serve with raita.

name: Tomato Rasam
steps: Boil the tomatoes in 2 cups of water for 5 minutes until soft, then mash them lightly.
Stir in the cooked toor dal, turmeric, crushed pepper, cumin and salt. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Heat ghee or oil, add mustard seeds; when they pop, add curry leaves, asafoetida and crushed garlic.
Pour the tempering into the rasam and simmer for 2 more minutes. Do not let it boil hard.
Garnish with coriander leaves and serve hot with rice or as a soup.

name: Chole Masala
steps: Pressure-cook the soaked chickpeas with salt for 4-5 whistles until soft. Keep the cooking water.
Heat oil, add cumin seeds, then onion. Fry until golden brown.
Add ginger, garlic and green chilli; fry a minute, then add tomato puree and the spice powders.
Cook the masala until the oil separates, then add the chickpeas with a cup of their cooking water.
Simmer for 10-15 minutes, mashing a few chickpeas to thicken the gravy.
Finish with garam masala and coriander leaves. Serve with bhature, roti or rice.

name: Palak Paneer
steps: Blanch the spinach in boiling water for 2 minutes, then plunge into cold water. Blend with the green chillies to a smooth puree.
Heat oil or ghee, add cumin seeds, then onion, garlic and ginger. Fry until the onion is soft.
Add tomato and cook until soft, then pour in the spinach puree and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add paneer cubes, garam masala and salt. Simmer for 3-4 minutes.
Stir in the cream and serve hot with roti or naan.

name: Jeera Rice
steps: Heat ghee in a pot. Add cumin seeds and bay leaf; fry until the seeds turn golden and fragrant.
Add the drained rice and stir gently for a minute so every grain is coated.
Add 3 cups of water and salt, cover and cook on low for 15 minutes.
Rest for 5 minutes, remove the bay leaf and fluff with a fork.
Garnish with coriander leaves and serve with dal or curry.

name: Masala Omelette
steps: Whisk the eggs with salt, turmeric and red chilli powder until frothy.
Stir in the onion, tomato, green chilli and coriander leaves.
Melt butter in a pan on medium heat and pour in the egg mixture.
Cook until the base sets, then fold in half and cook for another minute.
Serve hot with toast or pav.

name: Aloo Paratha
steps: Knead the wheat flour with water and a pinch of salt into a soft dough. Rest for 15 minutes.
Mix the mashed potato with onion, green chilli, ginger, coriander leaves, red chilli powder, garam masala and salt.
Roll a dough ball into a small disc, place a portion of filling in the centre, seal and roll out gently.
Roast on a hot tawa, flipping once, until golden spots appear on both sides. Smear with butter or ghee.
Serve hot with curd, pickle or butter.

name: Vegetable Upma
steps: Dry-roast the semolina in a pan until it turns light golden and fragrant. Set aside.
Heat ghee, add mustard seeds; when they pop, add curry leaves, onion, ginger and green chilli.
Add the vegetables and fry for 3 minutes, then add 2.5 cups of water and salt and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat and sprinkle in the roasted semolina slowly, stirring constantly to avoid lumps.
Cover and cook on low for 3-4 minutes until the water is absorbed.
Fluff, garnish with coriander leaves and serve hot.

name: Poha
steps: Rinse the poha in a colander under running water for a few seconds, then drain and rest for 5 minutes. It should soften, not turn mushy.
Heat oil, add mustard seeds; when they pop, add curry leaves, peanuts and potato. Fry until the potato is cooked.
Add onion and green chilli; fry until the onion is soft.
Add turmeric and salt, then the softened poha. Mix gently and cook for 2-3 minutes.
Turn off the heat, squeeze in the lemon juice and garnish with coriander leaves. Serve hot.

name: Besan Chilla
steps: Whisk the besan with 3/4 cup of water into a smooth, pourable batter. Rest for 5 minutes.
Stir in the onion, tomato, green chilli, coriander leaves, turmeric, red chilli powder, cumin and salt.
Heat a greased tawa, pour a ladle of batter and spread into a thin round.
Cook until the edges lift and the base is golden, then flip and cook the other side.
Serve hot with green chutney or ketchup.

name: Rajma Masala
steps: Pressure-cook the soaked kidney beans with salt for 4-5 whistles until soft. Keep the cooking water.
Heat oil, add cumin seeds, then onion. Fry until deep golden.
Add ginger and garlic, fry a minute, then add the tomato puree and spice powders. Cook until the oil separates.
Add the beans with a cup of their cooking water and simmer for 15 minutes, mashing a few beans to thicken.
Finish with garam masala and coriander leaves. Serve with steamed rice.

name: Baingan Bharta
steps: Roast the brinjal directly over a flame (or in a hot oven at 220 C for 25 minutes), turning until the skin is charred and the flesh is soft.
Cool, peel off the skin and mash the flesh.
Heat oil, add cumin seeds, then onion, ginger, garlic and green chilli. Fry until the onion is golden.
Add tomato, turmeric and red chilli powder. Cook until the tomato softens.
Stir in the mashed brinjal and salt. Cook for 5-7 minutes until everything comes together.
Garnish with coriander leaves and serve with roti.

name: Bhindi Masala
steps: Wash and thoroughly dry the okra, then cut it. Dry okra stays crisp and does not turn slimy.
Fry the okra in hot oil for 4-5 minutes until lightly browned. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, add cumin seeds, then onion, ginger and garlic. Fry until the onion is soft.
Add tomato and the spice powders. Cook until the tomato breaks down.
Return the okra to the pan, add salt and garam masala, and toss for 2 minutes. Serve with roti.

name: Curd Rice
steps: Mash the warm cooked rice lightly and let it cool to room temperature.
Mix in the curd and milk until creamy. Add salt.
Heat oil, add mustard seeds; when they pop, add curry leaves, green chilli and ginger.
Pour the tempering over the rice and mix well.
Garnish with coriander leaves and serve with pickle.

name: Lemon Rice
steps: Heat oil, add mustard seeds; when they pop, add curry leaves, peanuts and green chilli.
Add turmeric and asafoetida, then the cooked rice and salt. Toss gently so the grains stay separate.
Turn off the heat and stir in the lemon juice.
Garnish with coriander leaves and serve with papad or pickle.

name: Tomato Rice
steps: Heat oil, add cumin seeds, then onion, garlic and green chilli. Fry until the onion is soft.
Add tomato, red chilli powder and salt. Cook until the tomato turns pulpy and the oil separates.
Add the drained rice and garam masala, stir for a minute, then add 3 cups of water.
Cover and cook on low for 15 minutes until the rice is done.
Rest 5 minutes, fluff and garnish with coriander leaves. Serve with raita.

name: Chicken Curry
steps: Marinate the chicken with curd, turmeric, half the red chilli powder and salt for 15 minutes.
Heat oil, add onion and fry until deep golden. Add ginger, garlic and green chilli; fry for a minute.
Add tomato puree, coriander powder and remaining red chilli powder. Cook until the oil separates.
Add the chicken and fry on high for 5 minutes until it changes colour.
Add 1.5 cups of water, cover and simmer for 25 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Stir in garam masala and coriander leaves. Serve with rice or roti.

name: Egg Fried Rice
steps: Heat oil in a wok on high heat. Pour in the beaten eggs and scramble quickly. Remove and set aside.
In the same wok, fry garlic, onion, carrot, capsicum and peas for 2-3 minutes on high heat.
Add the cold rice and toss well so the grains stay separate.
Stir in soy sauce, black pepper and salt. Add the scrambled egg and toss for a minute.
Serve hot, garnished with spring onion if you have it.

name: Paneer Bhurji
steps: Heat oil, add cumin seeds, then onion, ginger and green chilli. Fry until the onion is soft.
Add tomato, capsicum, turmeric and red chilli powder. Cook until the tomato softens.
Add the crumbled paneer and salt. Cook for 3-4 minutes, stirring gently.
Finish with garam masala and coriander leaves. Serve with roti, pav or toast.

name: Moong Dal Khichdi
steps: Rinse the rice and moong dal together and soak for 15 minutes.
Heat ghee in a pressure cooker, add cumin seeds, then onion and ginger. Fry until soft.
Add tomato, carrot, peas and turmeric. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add the drained rice and dal with 4 cups of water and salt.
Pressure-cook for 3-4 whistles until soft and porridge-like. Serve hot with a spoon of ghee, curd or pickle.

name: Masala Dosa
steps: Heat oil, add mustard seeds; when they pop, add curry leaves, onion, ginger and green chilli.
Add turmeric and the mashed potato with salt. Mix well and cook for 2 minutes. This is the masala filling.
Heat a greased dosa tawa, pour a ladle of batter and spread in a spiral into a thin circle.
Drizzle a little oil around the edges and cook until crisp and golden.
Place a spoon of potato masala in the centre, fold the dosa over and serve hot with chutney and sambar.

name: Pav Bhaji
steps: Boil the potato, cauliflower and peas until soft, then mash them together.
Heat butter, add onion, ginger and garlic. Fry until the onion is golden.
Add capsicum and tomato. Cook until the tomato is pulpy.
Add pav bhaji masala and the mashed vegetables. Mix and cook for 10 minutes, mashing as you go.
Add water for the right consistency, finish with lemon juice and coriander leaves.
Toast pav in butter and serve alongside the bhaji with chopped onion and a lemon wedge.

name: Kadhi
steps: Whisk the curd with besan, turmeric and 2 cups of water until smooth with no lumps.
Heat oil, add cumin and mustard seeds; when they pop, add curry leaves, asafoetida, onion, ginger and green chilli.
Pour in the curd mixture and stir continuously until it comes to a gentle boil.
Simmer on low for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it thickens slightly.
Sprinkle red chilli powder and serve hot with steamed rice.

name: Methi Paratha
steps: Knead the wheat flour with fenugreek leaves, curd, green chilli, ginger, turmeric, red chilli powder and salt into a soft dough. Rest 15 minutes.
Divide into balls and roll each into a round paratha.
Roast on a hot tawa, flipping once, until golden spots appear on both sides. Smear with ghee.
Serve hot with curd or pickle.

name: Soya Chunk Curry
steps: Boil the soya chunks in salted water for 5 minutes, then rinse in cold water and squeeze out all the water.
Heat oil, add onion and fry until golden. Add ginger and garlic; fry for a minute.
Add tomato puree, turmeric, red chilli powder and coriander powder. Cook until the oil separates.
Add the soya chunks, curd and 1 cup of water. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Finish with garam masala and coriander leaves. Serve with rice or roti.

name: Tomato Soup
steps: Melt butter, add onion, garlic and carrot. Fry for 3 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and 2 cups of water. Simmer for 15 minutes until the tomatoes are soft.
Cool slightly and blend until smooth. Strain for a silky texture.
Return to the pan, add sugar, salt and black pepper, and simmer for 3 minutes.
Serve hot with a swirl of cream and toast or croutons.

name: Grilled Cheese Sandwich
steps: Butter one side of each bread slice.
Place cheese (and tomato, if using) between two slices, buttered sides out.
Grill in a pan on medium heat until golden and crisp on the first side.
Flip and grill the other side until the cheese melts.
Cut diagonally and serve hot.

name: Mushroom Masala
steps: Heat oil, add cumin seeds, then onion, ginger, garlic and green chilli. Fry until the onion is golden.
Add tomato, turmeric and red chilli powder. Cook until the tomato softens and the oil separates.
Add the mushrooms and salt. Cook on medium heat for 8-10 minutes until the mushrooms release and reabsorb their water.
Sprinkle garam masala and coriander leaves. Serve with roti or rice.

name: Cabbage Poriyal
steps: Heat oil, add mustard seeds; when they pop, add curry leaves and green chilli.
Add the cabbage, carrot, turmeric and salt. Sprinkle a little water and cover.
Cook on low for 8-10 minutes until the cabbage is tender but still has bite.
Stir in the grated coconut and cook for one more minute.
Serve hot with rice and sambar or rasam.

name: Mixed Vegetable Curry
steps: Heat oil, add cumin seeds, then onion, ginger and garlic. Fry until the onion is golden.
Add tomato, turmeric and coriander powder. Cook until the oil separates.
Add all the vegetables with 1 cup of water and salt. Cover and simmer for 15-20 minutes until tender.
Stir in garam masala and coriander leaves. Serve with roti or rice.
